changes: Removed the global official catalog value/promise cache and its independent refresh event. Settings and voice use one account/scope-owned hook and the existing verified key-change event. Only relay credential/address changes refresh the catalog; refresh aborts the previous request and late results cannot overwrite the new directory.

Official catalog metadata uses the existing backend type, validates rendering-relevant model/role fields, and stays null on failed or malformed reads. Closing, changing identity or work scope cancels the request; reopening performs a fresh read rather than reusing an old account cache.

Voice provider status and updates share one request lifecycle. A successful POST already returns pref and active, so the extra status GET, catalog GET and intent-based fallback event are deleted. The change event carries only a validated backend confirmation.

STT/TTS controls share a role-driven renderer and save function. Provider selection sends only its own role, and model selection only its own model field. Switching a provider leaves the other role and backend model/default selection intact.

Voice model selectors preserve the confirmed explicit model or effective server default when a directory is absent or omits it. The first catalog entry no longer replaces the effective default shown by the server.

Ordinary accounts do not mount privileged voice controls or fetch their status/catalog. Account/work-scope changes remount voice and settings state, aborting old operations. Repeated writes are blocked per view and failures retain the last confirmed selection.
Settings provider-status refreshes now cancel earlier reads, validate responses, clear failed results and have a 15-second signal instead of allowing old responses to overwrite newer provider status.

Official role apply reuses useModelOperation for serialization, cancellation and status. Its configuration event still refreshes AppContext but no longer remounts its own settings receipt, preserving displayed outcomes.
validationNotes: Six new behavior cases cover official apply publication/cancellation, settings provider refresh and receipt lifetime, in-flight official catalog replacement/key filtering/reopen, catalog identity/scope isolation, confirmed voice writes/default model display, and voice permission/failure/logout behavior.

Existing provider/relay tests now observe the canonical keys-changed event instead of the deleted catalog-specific event. One source-text-only privilege test and obsolete disabled-flag/voice-option source assertions were replaced by mounted behavior coverage.

Catalog and voice tests mount the actual hook/components and use the real authenticated API transport with synthetic fetch. Settings and official apply tests execute production functions with substituted layout/child components; HTTP integration suites use isolated databases and mock upstreams.

Initial UI test failures were missing fixture globals/constants (window, CustomEvent and documentation URL), not production failures. Final validation ran after correcting fixtures and after adding effective backend-default model display.
All 16 focused files, lint/type checks, all-frontend and desktop builds, and compact-layout checks passed. Final fingerprints preserve the latest prune40-66 baselines.
limitations: The common catalog hook owns one read per mounted consumer; it deliberately retains no global cache and does not deduplicate separately mounted consumers or cache across page visits. No upstream latency benchmark was performed.

Catalog failures keep existing documented fallback lists for model settings, and a saved/effective voice model remains selectable even if metadata omits it; the backend still decides whether a requested model is permitted. Catalog retry occurs on reopening, identity/scope change or a verified relay-key change.

Voice preferences remain the existing instance-wide administrator configuration. View/account isolation does not create per-user backend voice storage or cross-window transactions, and confirmation does not add stronger disk durability than the existing endpoint provides.
Canceling frontend requests cannot undo server-accepted updates. Fifteen-second signals bound fetch waiting; they do not cancel upstream work already executing on the backend.
No full-suite run, real provider/credential or user-data operation, microphone/audio playback acceptance, native GUI acceptance, backend rebuild, commit, push or client restart.
